__meta.what: Golden file for canonical serialisation (src/core/canonical.ts). PROP-W1 and DET-4.
__meta.why: terms_hash is what two principals countersign. If the same logical terms can serialise two ways, agents see hash mismatches and correctly read them as a counterparty reneging - the engine fabricating a betrayal, which is the A5-prime failure and worse than a crash.
__meta.cross_platform: This file IS the cross-platform contract for DET-4. One test process cannot run two operating systems, so instead every platform must reproduce these exact strings and hashes. A Linux CI run failing this test is DET-4 firing.
__meta.hash: sha256 of the canonical string, hex - verifiable without running engine code
__meta.regenerate: The canonical column is hand-authored and is the oracle; the hash column is derived from it. A diff here is either a deliberate canonicaliser version bump (CANONICAL_VERSION must change in the same commit) or a bug.
__meta.ascii_only: Non-ASCII is written as \uXXXX so NFC/NFD pairs and lone surrogates are unambiguous on inspection.
__meta.not_here: Minus zero, undefined-valued keys, symbol keys and inherited keys are unrepresentable in JSON (JSON.stringify(-0) is "0"), so they live in canonical-edge.json with their inputs built in test/golden/edge-values.ts.

cases.name: scalar_null
cases.note: null is a value, distinct from absent

cases.name: scalar_true
cases.note: booleans are bare words, never 0/1

cases.name: scalar_false
cases.note: booleans are bare words, never 0/1

cases.name: scalar_zero
cases.note: plain integer

cases.name: scalar_negative_integer
cases.note: sign is part of the digits, no separate marker

cases.name: scalar_max_safe_integer
cases.note: the largest Minor that may be hashed; no exponent notation at any magnitude

cases.name: scalar_min_safe_integer
cases.note: the most negative Minor that may be hashed

cases.name: scalar_empty_string
cases.note: an empty string is a value

cases.name: empty_object
cases.note: an empty object is not an empty array

cases.name: empty_array
cases.note: an empty array is not an empty object

cases.name: empty_structures_nested
cases.note: empty containers nest without collapsing into each other

cases.name: key_order_ascii
cases.note: insertion order b,a,c must serialise a,b,c

cases.name: key_order_numeric_like
cases.note: THE numeric-key determinism killer (SPEC 15.5): JSON.stringify emits 1,2,10 — code-unit order is 1,10,2

cases.name: key_order_numeric_mixed
cases.note: V8 puts integer-like keys first in Object.keys whatever the insertion order; sorting must override that

cases.name: key_order_prefixed_numeric
cases.note: k1,k2,k10 sort as k1,k10,k2 — the same trap once a prefix hides it

cases.name: key_order_case_sensitive
cases.note: uppercase sorts before lowercase by code unit; a locale collation would not

cases.name: key_order_punctuation
cases.note: hyphen < digit < uppercase < underscore < lowercase, by code unit only

cases.name: key_order_prefix_shorter_first
cases.note: a prefix sorts before its extensions; the empty key sorts first of all

cases.name: key_order_unicode
cases.note: non-ASCII keys sort by UTF-16 code unit, so no ICU version can move them

cases.name: string_escapes
cases.note: quote and backslash escape; forward slash does not

cases.name: string_control_chars
cases.note: short escapes for b,f,n,r,t and lowercase \u00xx for the rest — pinned because a raw byte here would be unparseable

cases.name: string_lone_surrogate
cases.note: a lone surrogate escapes to \udxxx (well-formed stringify), never raw bytes

cases.name: string_astral_and_zwj
cases.note: astral planes and a zero-width joiner pass through raw; the byte sequence is what is pinned

cases.name: string_unicode_normalisation_is_not_applied
cases.note: NFC e-acute and NFD e+combining-acute are DIFFERENT terms and hash differently — deliberate, but agents must be told

cases.name: string_digits_are_not_integers
cases.note: the string "1" must not collide with the integer 1

cases.name: int_looks_like_the_digit_string
cases.note: paired with string_digits_are_not_integers; the two hashes must differ

cases.name: delimiter_injection_attempt
cases.note: a key carrying the structural delimiters must not be able to forge a second field

cases.name: delimiter_injection_target
cases.note: the shape the previous case tries to impersonate; the hashes must differ

cases.name: array_order_is_meaning
cases.note: arrays are sequences: order is preserved, never sorted

cases.name: array_heterogeneous
cases.note: every scalar kind and both containers side by side

cases.name: array_of_objects_keys_sorted_elements_not
cases.note: element order stays, key order sorts — two different rules in one structure

cases.name: null_valued_key_is_present
cases.note: paired with the constructed case where b is undefined and disappears entirely

cases.name: deep_nested_32
cases.note: 32 levels is the documented maximum and must serialise; 33 throws (asserted in code)

cases.name: venture_terms_realistic
cases.note: a plausible terms_hash input: integer Minor, integer Bps, wage XOR share, valuation rule pinned with its as-of tick (SPEC 15.4)
